candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes classic histoid leprosy features: discrete firm cutaneous nodules, storiform arrangement of foamy histiocytes with grenz zone, abundant AFB (BI 4.8), and mild hypoaesthesia without nerve thickening. Histoid leprosy is a distinct clinicopathological variant of multibacillary leprosy (often associated with dapsone resistance or relapse), so 'multibacillary leprosy' is a compatible parent category but lacks the required histoid subtype specificity demanded by the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Multibacillary leprosy is the parent category that includes histoid leprosy, but does not capture the specific histoid subtype with its distinctive storiform foamy histiocyte pattern, discrete firm nodules, and high bacterial index characteristic of histoid leprosy

case_quality_flags: Neighbor contact history (ages 3-18) supports childhood leprosy exposure consistent with long incubation

Autoantibody positivity (ANA, anti-Ro52, anti-cardiolipin, elevated RF) may represent leprosy-associated immunological phenomena and could have led to misdiagnosis as connective tissue disease, explaining prior ineffective hydroxychloroquine/thalidomide treatment
